title: Penetration testing: are you testing what attackers target, and fixing what testers find?
short: Scope tests around identity, internet-facing systems and critical apps, and fix and retest critical and high findings within 30 days.
answer: Before the next test, write down the question it must answer and scope it around identity, internet-facing systems and critical apps, not an IP list. Judge each test by how many findings were fixed and retested on time.
audience: IT, security and engineering leads in EU organizations, many in Germany, who commission penetration tests or red team exercises, or must under DORA or PCI DSS

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Start from a question, not a product.
items.text: The NCSC treats a penetration test as an audit of your vulnerability management: you should already know most of what it finds[^ncscpt]. Write down the question the test must answer.

items.title: Scope by attacker targets.
items.text: Exploits opened 32% of Mandiant's 2025 intrusions and voice phishing 11%, with groups calling help desks to get past MFA[^mtrends]. Scope identity, the help desk, the edge and critical apps first.

items.title: Give testers the inside view.
items.text: The BSI recommends white-box tests, since black-box tests miss more and risk more damage[^bsipt]. Hand over network plans, test accounts, source code and your latest vulnerability assessment[^ncscpt].

items.title: Get written authorization from every owner.
items.text: The BSI says never to test without a written contract, and to include any hoster[^bsipt]. Microsoft won't authorize testers for you[^azpt].

items.title: Retest and track every finding to closure.
items.text: PCI DSS requires a retest to verify fixes[^pci] and DORA a check that every weakness is addressed[^dora]. Give each finding an owner and a deadline, and book the retest with the test.

blocks.title: Commission a test in this order

items.title: Agree the scope with the risk owner.
items.text: Involve risk owners, technical staff and the testers, and agree boundaries, test types, effort in days and reporting[^ncscpt].

items.title: Get everyone's consent.
items.text: The system owner, any hoster or SaaS provider and, if staff or personal data are affected, the data protection officer and works council[^bsipt].

items.title: Set the rules of engagement.
items.text: Agree the window, exclusions, depth, a stop rule and a contact on call[^ncscpt]. Freeze changes in scope; if a flaw can't wait, pause the test[^bsipt].

items.title: Read the report critically.
items.text: The risk decision is yours[^ncscpt]. Group findings by cause[^bsipt] and ask why you didn't already know about each one[^ncscpt].

items.title: Close the loop.
items.text: Fix by deadline, retest and add each finding to your own regular checks[^bsipt]. Removing the software or adding monitoring may beat the suggested patch[^ncscpt].

blocks.title: Pick the test that answers your question
items: **Vulnerability scan: which known flaws are open?** Automated and frequent; see the attack surface sheet. A penetration test adds a competent manual attacker[^pci].
**Penetration test: does this system hold up against a skilled tester?** Days of manual work on one system with full information, after go-live and significant changes[^bsipt].
**Assumed breach: how far does one compromised laptop or account get?** The tester starts inside, as in the NCSC's lost laptop scenario[^ncscpt].

**Red team: would you detect and stop a real attacker?** A covert, threat-led attack on live systems; under DORA the active phase lasts at least 12 weeks[^rts]. Wait until logging and alert handling work.
**Purple teaming: which attacker techniques do you detect?** Testers and defenders work together and tune detections as they go. DORA requires it after every threat-led test[^rts].
**Bug bounty: what do outsiders find over time?** See the secure development sheet.

blocks.title: Scope by risk, not by IP list
items: **Identity.** Paths from a normal user to domain admin or Global Administrator, including AD CS; the privileged access sheet lists fixes.
**The help desk.** A call asking for an MFA reset, under rules agreed with the works council and run by specialists[^bsipt].
**The internet edge and critical apps.** Everything in the attack surface sheet's inventory, and apps tested as the API security sheet describes.
**Backups, hypervisors and tenants.** Ransomware groups target backups and virtualization management[^mtrends]; Microsoft encourages tenant tests[^azpt].
**How often.** Test high-risk areas yearly and after major changes. The BSI suggests repeating tests every two to three years[^bsipt].

blocks.title: Choose a provider
items: **Treat certificates as signals.** PCI DSS calls them an indication of skill and asks about past engagements too[^pci]. BSI personnel certification and CREST include practical exams[^bsipt].
**In Germany, check the BSI list.** It names 22 providers certified for IS penetration tests[^bsilist].
**In UK government and CNI, use CHECK.** Its team leaders hold the UK Cyber Security Council's Principal title and SC clearance[^check].
**Buy the people, not the logo.** Get CVs of the named testers, at least two, check they do the work and rotate them over the years[^bsipt].

blocks.title: Stay legal and safe
items: **Authorization.** In Germany, unauthorized access to protected data carries up to three years in prison[^stgb].

**Cloud.** On Azure, AWS and Google Cloud, most tests of your own resources need no notice[^azpt][^aws][^gcp]. Azure and AWS ban DoS tests; AWS wants two weeks' notice of covert red teaming or phishing[^aws].
**Production and OT.** No test can rule out side effects[^ncscpt], so keep a stop rule. For OT, hire testers with OT experience[^ncsccni].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **AI-assisted testing needs ground rules.** The NCSC's 10 questions from May 2026 cover who fixes the findings, sandboxing, data terms and legality[^ncscai]. Ask testers who use AI the same.
**CREST accredits AI security testing.** It named the first four companies in November 2026[^crestai]. Ask for it, or comparable evidence, before testing a GenAI or LLM system.

blocks.title: Tests a regulation or contract requires
blocks.intro: NIS2 requires checks that security measures work[^nis2], and a risk-based testing policy for cloud and managed service providers[^nis2ir]. DORA requires yearly tests of systems behind critical or important functions[^dora].

items.name: DORA threat-led penetration test (TLPT)
items.scope: Entities their authority selects, at least every 3 years, on live systems[^dora]. In Germany the Bundesbank runs tests BaFin or the ECB orders[^tiberde]. Clocks start at the notice, then at the end of red teaming[^rts].

items.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1, requirement 11.4
items.scope: The card data environment, by a qualified, organizationally independent tester who needn't be a QSA[^pci]. For segmentation tests, see the network segmentation sheet.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Black-box tests for realism.** Testers then spend paid days finding out what you could tell them. The BSI recommends white-box tests[^bsipt].
**A red team before the basics.** If scans still find unpatched edge systems and nobody handles alerts, a red team only confirms it, at a high price.
**External retests of low findings.** Retest critical and high findings with the testers and check the rest yourself[^bsipt].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Taking a clean report as proof.** PCI DSS says a test that finds nothing usually reflects the tester's shortcomings[^pci]; see the edge devices sheet.
**Letting the WAF test itself.** If it blocks the testers, you test the filter. Lift the blocks for them and test the gateway separately[^bsipt].
**Leaving the testers' tools behind.** DORA makes testers remove backdoors and delete captured credentials[^rts]; demand the same.
**Findings without an owner.** Risk decisions stay with you, not the testers[^ncscpt].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Test your cloud tenant and internet edge yearly.
Fix and retest critical and high findings in 30 days.
Shortlist from the BSI list or CREST.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Test AD and Entra ID yearly from a user's laptop.
Test critical app releases with source code.
Report open findings by age every month.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Plan tests by risk for several years ahead.
Map the plan to DORA[^dora] and PCI DSS 11.4[^pci].
Report time to close to the board.
